title: fix(unigram): stabilize required-character finalization order
body:
## Problem

Unigram finalization iterates required characters in hash-set order. Equal-score characters receive hash-dependent token IDs; required characters absent from the learned vocabulary also receive hash-dependent fallback penalties. Identical learned pieces can therefore be finalized into different vocabularies.

## Change

Visit required characters in a stable sorted order before assigning fallback penalties and applying the existing stable score sort. Special-token order, learned scores, candidate selection and EM updates retain their existing behavior. Freshly trained equal-score character IDs become stable; loading an existing model does not run this finalization step.

## Validation

Native Rust on Ubuntu with Rust 1.100.0, at the exact contribution SHA:

- 6 new tests pass. Restoring unchanged upstream gives 5 failures and 1 passing control.
- All 5 existing Unigram trainer tests pass.
- Fixed hash seeds are checked against explicit token-ID and fallback-score expectations. Tests also cover native repeated training, Unicode token offsets, unseen initial alphabets, requested special-token order/unknown ID and distinct-score controls.
- Changed Rust files pass rustfmt.
- Strict Clippy is blocked by the same two pre-existing `needless_range_loop` diagnostics in unchanged upstream and patched code (`word_cache.rs` and `unigram/lattice.rs`).

Run: https://github.com/Afloat16/tokenizers/actions/runs/43298508797

The scope is nondeterminism introduced by required-character iteration during finalization. This does not promise identical floating-point reductions across all parallel EM training configurations.
